subject: Linetype 3 goes missing in my figures

messages.author: 46983456658f45c9
messages.subject: Linetype 3 goes missing in my figures
parts:
Hi

Lintype 3 does not show up in my figures. I have seen a bunch of posts
on this, but I didn't see any final response.

So, when I let ggplot pick the linetype, or when I manually set the
linetype using
+ scale_linetype_manual(color.caption,values=c(1,2,3,4,5))
the linetype 3 does not show up in my pdf file.

When I use
+scale_linetype_manual(color.caption,values=c(1,2,4,5,6)
everything shows up.

It seems linetype 3 has a problem. Any tips?
(the reason I am looking for a solution is because I would rather
avoid setting the types manually).

I am on a 64-bit Linux machine and using R version 2.10.1

Thanks
Siavash

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Linetype 3 goes missing in my figures
parts:
Hi:

Works for me. Here's a reproducible example:

dd <- data.frame(x = 1:10, x1 = rnorm(10), x2 = rnorm(10),
x3 = rnorm(10), x4 = rnorm(10), y = rnorm(10))
ddm <- melt(dd, id = 'x')

# Not in order of linetypes, but works
ggplot(ddm, aes(x = x, y = value, linetype = variable)) + geom_line()

ggplot(ddm, aes(x = x, y = value, linetype = variable)) + geom_line()
# works
last_plot() + scale_linetype_manual(breaks = levels(ddm$variable),
values = c('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash'))
# same as above
last_plot() + scale_linetype_manual(breaks = levels(ddm$variable),
values = 1:5)

You've got an ancient version of R and ggplot2 is under very active
development, so I would strongly urge you to upgrade to the latest
versions of R and ggplot2.

On Tue, Aug 23, 2011 at 9:37 AM, siavash mirarab <smir...@gmail.com> wrote:

> c('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash'))
> dev.off()
> Can you test this code as well?

I ran the following:

# Method 1: Use ggsave() from ggplot2:
ggplot(ddm, aes(x = x, y = value, linetype = variable)) + geom_line() +

ggsave('test1.pdf')

# Method 2: Open a pdf device, print the plot, close the device:
pdf('test2.pdf')
print(ggplot(ddm, aes(x = x, y = value, linetype = variable)) + geom_line() +
scale_linetype_manual(breaks = levels(ddm$variable),
values = c('solid', 'dashed', 'dotted', 'dotdash', 'longdash')) )
dev.off()

The two graphs are identical, so I uploaded the second one. The dotted
lines (x3) show up in both saved pdf plots. I'm using version 10.1.0
of Adobe Reader with the same R setup reported in my previous reply.

> If the pdf shows correctly for you, then the problem is with my ancient R
> version.

That's one possibility; another is that your PDF reader might be the
problem. A number of reports about pdf output from R not being
rendered properly in certain viewers have been made to R-help over the
past year or so. I'm not up to date on the specific details of that
problem, so if you want to pursue that route you could search the
R-help archives.

Since ggplot2 is in very active development, you should ideally
maintain an R version that is up to date. It's unclear which version
of Linux you have installed, but if it's recent, the package/update
manager does a pretty good job of keeping R up to date.

HTH,
Dennis
